findings.title: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException on missing English file, crashing the Maven build
findings.body: When the English counterpart file (computed via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community","resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties","_en.properties")`) does not exist, the catch block wraps the `FileNotFoundException` as `new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e)`. The caller `verify()` only catches `IOException` (line 52), so the `RuntimeException` propagates and aborts the Maven build with an uncaught-exception stack trace instead of a clean Mojo-level error. For any property file under `resources-community` whose English sibling is missing or whose path does not match the assumed layout, the theme-verifier plugin will crash. The fix is to declare `throws MojoExecutionException` on `verifySafeHtml` (or wrap the call into `try { … } catch (IOException|RuntimeException e) { throw new MojoExecutionException(..., e); }` in `verify()`).

findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The line was changed from the Lithuanian string `totpStep1=Įdiekite FreeOTP arba Google Authenticator savo įrenginyje. …` to `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. The new value is Italian, not Lithuanian, so users with the Lithuanian locale will see Italian text in the account UI. The sanitizer does not detect this because it only checks HTML structure, not translation correctness, and the corresponding English source (`Install one of the following applications on your mobile:`) has no HTML so POLICY_NO_HTML is used. The right value should be a Lithuanian translation of the English source.

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: Same regression as in the account bundle: `loginTotpStep1=Įdiekite FreeOTP arba Google Authenticator savo įrenginyje. …` was replaced by `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the login TOTP step-up page.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle uses Traditional Chinese characters
findings.body: The new `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` mixes Traditional-only characters (`機`, `裝`, `應用`, `程式`) into the zh-CN resource bundle, which is supposed to be Simplified Chinese. The rest of the file is Simplified. Mixing scripts causes inconsistent rendering depending on the viewer's font fallback chain and breaks the zh-CN/zh-TW separation. The expected translation should use Simplified forms (手机, 安装, 应用, 程序).

findings.title: HTML_TAGS regex is case-sensitive and misses uppercase tags
findings.body:
`Pattern HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>");` only matches lower-case tag names. Real-world translations can use mixed-case or upper-case tags (e.g., `
`, `

`). When the English source uses such tags, `containsHtml` returns false, `POLICY_NO_HTML` is selected instead of `POLICY_SOME_HTML`, and legitimate allowed elements such as `
` in the translation get stripped, producing a false "Illegal HTML" error. Either compile the pattern with `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE` or use `[a-zA-Z]+`.

findings.title: Locale-matching regex includes unintended characters due to misplaced `-`
findings.body: The pattern `"_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties"` contains the character class `[a-zA-Z-_]`. Java's regex interprets the `-` between `Z` and `_` as a range, so the class actually matches `a-z`, `A-Z`, `[`, `\\`, `]`, `^`, `_`. For typical locale codes (`de`, `zh_CN`, etc.) this happens to work, but a malformed locale segment could be accepted. Move the `-` to the end of the class to make it literal: `_[a-zA-Z_-]*\\.properties`.

findings.title: PolicyFactory instances are not static final
findings.body: `POLICY_SOME_HTML` and `POLICY_NO_HTML` are non-static instance fields initialized in each `VerifyMessageProperties` instance, and are declared after the constructor and `verify()` method. They are immutable and shared between instances, so they should be `private static final`. This avoids rebuilding the OWASP policies for every file checked and makes the intent explicit.

findings.title: Typo in method name: 'santizeAnchors' should be 'sanitizeAnchors'
findings.body: The helper that strips matching anchor tags is misspelled `santizeAnchors` (missing the second `i`). Rename to `sanitizeAnchors`.

findings.title: getEnglishValue silently swallows MissingResourceException
findings.body: If a key is present in the translation bundle but missing from the English bundle, `getEnglishValue` catches `MissingResourceException` and returns the empty string. The sanitizer then evaluates the translation against `englishValue=""`: `containsHtml` is false so `POLICY_NO_HTML` is used, which strips any HTML the translation has and produces a spurious "Illegal HTML" error. A missing English key should be reported as a separate problem (out-of-sync bundles) rather than masked as if English had no HTML for that key. Either rethrow `MissingResourceException` as a dedicated message or treat the missing-English-key case explicitly.
